# Kalshi Market Watchlist Tracker — 2026-07-19 through 2026-07-26

**Watchlist only. Generated by `whole_market_watchlist_tracker.py`, rerunnable as more
dates are added to a future `whole_market_exploration*.py` run.** This report does not
change model logic, thresholds, or lanes; does not promote any lane; does not create
trades, paper trades, Discord alerts, or write to live Slate Monitor outputs. It reads
the already-graded rows from the whole-market exploratory diagnostic
(`outputs/kalshi_import_reconstruction_audit/whole_market_exploration_2026-07-19_2026-07-26/whole_market_rows.csv`,
9,822 ticker-side rows across 110 games / 220 team-game rows / 6,236 distinct Kalshi
tickers / ~4.6M pregame snapshots) plus `kalshi_mlb.db` and the reconstructed pregame
cards, and rolls it into six recurring watchlist categories. `mlb_games.game_start_time_utc`
is the only pregame clock used anywhere upstream (never ticker `HHMM`). Doubleheader-ambiguous
games are excluded upstream, not guessed at.

Generated: 2026-07-28. Window covered: 2026-07-19 → 2026-07-26 (8 dates). Re-run this
script after more dates are added to widen the window; every output file carries
`generated_at` / `window_start` / `window_end` columns so a rerun is self-describing.

## 1. High-priced YES danger zone

Full detail: `watchlist_price_bucket_performance.csv` (also inside `watchlist_bucket_tracking.csv`
under `category=expensive_yes`), row-level in `kalshi_market_watchlist_rows.csv`
(`watchlist_category=expensive_yes`, 1,492 rows).

| price bucket | n | hit rate | breakeven | hit − breakeven | P/L (1 contract) | avg spread | avg snapshot age (min before start) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 56–65¢ | 350 | 54.0% | 60.3% | **-6.3pp** | **-2,206¢** | 4.20¢ | 0.9 |
| 66–80¢ | 456 | 71.3% | 73.0% | -1.7pp | -785¢ | 4.53¢ | 0.9 |
| 81–99¢ | 686 | 87.8% | 90.0% | -2.3pp | -1,554¢ | 6.82¢ | 0.9 |

By market type, the two worst-sampled cells both sit in the 56–65¢ bucket:

| price bucket | market type | n | hit rate | breakeven | gap | P/L | avg spread |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 56–65¢ | moneyline | 37 | 45.95% | 58.89% | **-12.95pp** | -479¢ | 2.83¢ |
| 56–65¢ | team totals | 136 | 53.68% | 60.52% | **-6.85pp** | -931¢ | 5.15¢ |
| 66–80¢ | team totals | 195 | 68.72% | 73.14% | -4.42pp | -862¢ | 4.87¢ |
| 81–99¢ | F5 totals | 224 | 87.50% | 91.23% | -3.73pp | -836¢ | 13.94¢ |

**Read:** the same pattern the original whole-market diagnostic flagged reproduces here —
YES 56–65¢ is still the worst pooled bucket (hit rate 6.3pp under its own breakeven,
worst total P/L per contract of the three), and it's driven by moneyline and team-total
YES specifically, not spread/F5 markets. Team totals also underperform breakeven at
66–80¢. Nothing here is new since the base report; this is the baseline this category
exists to track forward as more dates land.

## 3. Run-differential favorite/underdog context

Full detail: `watchlist_bucket_tracking.csv` under `category=run_differential_context`.
Classification: season run-differential-per-game gap (team's
`season_run_diff_pg_before_game` minus opponent's, from
`historical_team_context_preview_v2/historical_team_context_2026_clean.csv`, **not**
market price) — `stronger_team_vs_weaker_team` if gap > +0.3 runs/game,
`weaker_team_vs_stronger_team` if gap < -0.3, `roughly_even_matchup` otherwise (±0.3
threshold chosen from this window's gap distribution — std dev ≈ 1.0 run/game, so ±0.3
captures the flattest ~14% of matchups; a watchlist bucketing choice, not a model change).
Computed on YES rows across **all seven market types**, not moneyline-only.

| market type | context | n | hit rate | market implied prob | actual − implied | P/L |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| team totals | roughly_even | 168 | 56.5% | 47.9% | **+8.6pp** | **+1,325¢** |
| team totals | stronger vs weaker | 595 | 47.0% | 49.3% | -2.3pp | -1,299¢ |
| team totals | weaker vs stronger | 595 | 40.9% | 44.9% | -4.0pp | -2,289¢ |
| moneyline | stronger vs weaker | 85 | 54.9% | 54.8% | +0.1pp | +10¢ |
| moneyline | roughly_even | 24 | 50.0% | 50.6% | -0.6pp | -12¢ |
| moneyline | weaker vs stronger | 85 | 45.1% | 46.5% | -1.3pp | -110¢ |
| F5 winner | weaker vs stronger | 84 | 30.5% | 40.7% | **-10.2pp** | -838¢ |
| F5 winner | roughly_even | 24 | 50.0% | 43.4% | +6.6pp | +145¢ |
| runline/spread | stronger vs weaker | 549 | 25.4% | 29.1% | -3.7pp | -1,513¢ |

**Read:** two things stand out. (1) **`team totals` in the `roughly_even_matchup` bucket is
the single cleanest positive cell in this whole report** (+8.6pp actual-vs-implied, +1,325¢,
n=168) — when the two teams are evenly matched by season run differential, team-total YES
outcomes beat their market price by a wide margin. (2) **`F5 winner` for the weaker team
against a stronger opponent is the worst context cell found anywhere in this tracker**
(-10.2pp, -838¢, n=84) — weaker teams underperform their already-discounted F5-winner price.
The moneyline favorite/underdog split (matching the original report's section 6, at
n=97/side there vs n=85+24 here after the ±0.3 even-bucket carve-out) stays close to
breakeven at this finer three-way cut. Track `team totals × roughly_even` and
`F5 winner × weaker_vs_stronger` specifically as the window grows.

## 4. Brain-market disagreement

Full detail: `watchlist_brain_market_gap.csv` (558 row-level pairs — every team-game/market
row with both a brain calibrated probability and a usable market fill price, across the
three lane-aligned pairings: `side_score`/moneyline, `team_runs_4plus_score`/TEAM4-YES,
`team_runs_5plus_no_score`/TEAM5-NO). Bucketed on brain calibrated probability ≥/< 50% ×
market price ≥/< 50¢.

| bucket | n | hit rate | P/L |
|---|---|---|---|
| brain high / market high (both agree, likely) | 368 | 56.5% | **-1,163¢** |
| brain low / market low (both agree, unlikely) | 70 | 42.9% | -7¢ |
| brain high / market low (brain likes it, market doesn't) | 60 | 46.7% | +77¢ |
| brain low / market high (market likes it, brain doesn't) | 60 | 55.0% | +42¢ |

**Read:** exact reproduction of the base report's finding. The "everyone agrees it's
likely" bucket has a perfectly respectable hit rate (56.5%, comfortably above 50%) but is
the only bucket that loses real money (-1,163¢) — the price already had the likelihood
priced in, so a winning record still nets a loss. The two genuine-disagreement buckets are
both small (n=60 each) and close to breakeven in opposite directions — neither confirms nor
rules out the brain adding signal when it disagrees with the market. This is the pattern
most worth re-checking as sample size grows, since n=60 is too small to call either way yet.

## 5. Market drift

Full detail: `watchlist_bucket_tracking.csv` under `category=market_drift`
(`dimension_type` = `magnitude`, `direction`, or `magnitude_by_market_type`). Computed
YES-side only (buying NO to "fade" uses that ticker's own actual NO-side row, not a
synthetic mirror of the YES P/L — an actual fill, not an approximation). `pl_buy_early`
uses the first pregame snapshot price as the fill; `pl_buy_late` uses the realistic
last-pregame-snapshot fill (same convention as the rest of this report).

**By magnitude:**

| move size | n | hit rate | P/L buy early | P/L buy late | P/L fade (buy NO instead) | % moved toward winner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| flat (=0¢) | 424 | 54.5% | -692¢ | -692¢ | -19¢ | n/a |
| small (<5¢) | 1,443 | 56.5% | -28¢ | +1,334¢ | -3,888¢ | 51.6% |
| medium (5–10¢) | 446 | 46.0% | -3,399¢ | -889¢ | +71¢ | 59.2% |
| big (>10¢) | 1,888 | **34.1%** | **-87,026¢** | **-5,681¢** | **+1,325¢** | 66.0% |

**By direction (first → last price):**

| direction | n | hit rate | P/L buy early | P/L buy late |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| moved up | 521 | **63.5%** | +1,872¢ | +710¢ |
| flat | 424 | 54.5% | -692¢ | -692¢ |
| moved down | 3,256 | 40.9% | -92,325¢ | -5,946¢ |

**Read:** buying-early P/L is dramatically worse than buying-late P/L in the `moved down` /
`big move` buckets specifically (-92,325¢ vs -5,946¢ for moved-down; -87,026¢ vs -5,681¢
for big moves) — this is mechanical, not a new finding: these rows started at a materially
higher average price (69.3¢ avg first-price for moved-down rows) and mostly lost, so paying
the higher early price loses far more than paying the already-discounted late price. It is
**not** evidence that "buying early is bad" in general — it's an artifact of which contracts
happen to fall a lot (expensive ones that were already going to lose more often than not).
The genuinely interesting result, matching the base report: YES contracts that moved *up*
pregame won more often (63.5%) and were profitable to buy after the move at either the early
or late price, while big moves (>10¢) had only a 34.1% hit rate and lost badly to buy but
would have made money to fade (+1,325¢) — carrying the same structural caveat as before
(large listed-threshold markets have more room to fall than rise by construction, so this
is not yet a confirmed tradable "fade the move" signal).

## 6. Team coverage gaps

Full detail: `watchlist_team_coverage_gaps.csv` (220 team-game rows — the full
reconstructed-pregame-card universe for this window, 2 rows per game).

| coverage_gap_type | team-game rows | games |
|---|---|---|
| ok_has_usable_price | 186 | 93 |
| no_kalshi_ticker_match | 14 | 7 |
| doubleheader_ambiguous_excluded | 12 | 6 |
| no_pregame_snapshot | 8 | 4 |

**`no_kalshi_ticker_match` (14 rows / 7 games) — all 7 are Washington Nationals games**,
confirmed again this rerun: 2026-07-19 WSN@ATH, 2026-07-20/21/22 WSN@COL, 2026-07-24/25/26
AZ@WSN. This is a real Kalshi-side listing gap, not a join bug (`WSN` is the correct
abbreviation used consistently in `mlb_games`; no `WAS`-style mismatch found).

**`no_pregame_snapshot` (8 rows / 4 games) — all four games are from 2026-07-19**
(CWS@TOR, NYM@PHI, TB@BOS, TEX@ATL): 2026-07-19 is flagged
`partial_day_collection_started_1737z` in `kalshi_import_coverage_by_date.csv` — collection
started mid-afternoon that day, so early games missed pregame collection entirely. This is
a **collection-timing gap for one specific day**, not a Kalshi listing gap and not specific
to any team — distinct in cause from the WSN gap above.

**`doubleheader_ambiguous_excluded` (12 rows / 6 games, 3 date-team pairs):** 2026-07-19
LAD@NYY, 2026-07-22 PIT@NYY, 2026-07-22 BAL@BOS — excluded by design (both legs), not
guessed at from ticker text.

**Read:** coverage gaps are concentrated by two independent causes, not one: WSN listing
gaps (team-specific, persistent across the whole window) and one bad collection day
(date-specific, not team-specific). Both should be tracked separately going forward —
if WSN gaps persist into new dates, that's a durable Kalshi-side gap worth flagging up;
if `no_pregame_snapshot` reappears on other dates for other teams, that points at
collection infrastructure rather than Kalshi's listings.

## Handoff for Atlas and Justin

**Which watchlist buckets are currently most interesting?** `team totals ×
roughly_even_matchup` (run-differential context, section 3): +8.6pp actual-vs-implied,
+1,325¢, n=168 — the cleanest positive cell in this tracker. Also worth watching: TEAM5 NO
against a weak (<8 K-BB%) opposing starter (+461¢, n=70) and against a 45–50 offense-form
team (+384¢, n=66), both context cuts rather than score cuts (section 2).

**Which buckets are losing despite good hit rate?** The brain-market "both agree it's
likely" bucket (56.5% hit rate but -1,163¢, n=368, section 4) and the whole-market YES
56–65¢ bucket (54.0% hit rate, still below its own 60.3¢ breakeven, -2,206¢, n=350,
section 1) — both reproduce the base report's core finding that a winning record can still
lose money once price is accounted for.

**Is Team Runs 5+ NO still positive?** Not clearly. Overall P/L across all 194 TEAM5 NO
rows in this window is essentially flat (-59¢, 57.5% hit rate vs 57.8% breakeven — a
-0.32pp gap, statistical noise). More importantly, **zero rows in this window qualify as
official candidates** under the lane's real `score >= 0.40` rule (max score seen: 0.32) —
the "early promise" language from the base report describes a different, longer-history
sample (`team_runs_5plus_no_logic_audit.py`), not this 8-date window specifically. Track
whether qualifying candidates start appearing as more dates are added.

**Does run-differential context still look useful?** Yes, more so than before — breaking
it out by market type (not moneyline-only, section 3) surfaces `team totals ×
roughly_even_matchup` as the single cleanest edge-shaped cell in this entire tracker, and
`F5 winner × weaker_vs_stronger` as the single worst context cell (-10.2pp, -838¢, n=84).
Both deserve continued tracking; neither is proven at n=84-168 on one 8-day window.

**Does the brain add value when it disagrees with the market?** Still inconclusive. Both
disagreement buckets (n=60 each) sit close to breakeven in opposite directions. The
agreement bucket (brain high / market high) continues to look like the brain mostly
flagging things the market already priced up, not finding edges the market missed.

**Are expensive YES markets still dangerous?** Yes. YES 56–65¢ remains the worst-gapped
bucket (-6.3pp, -2,206¢, n=350), driven specifically by moneyline (-12.95pp, n=37) and team
totals (-6.85pp, n=136) at that price level. YES 66–80¢ team totals also underperform
(-4.42pp, -862¢, n=195).

**Are coverage gaps concentrated by team or market type?** By team for one cause (WSN, 7/7
zero-coverage games are Nationals games) and by date for a separate cause (all 8
no-pregame-snapshot rows are from the one partial-collection day, 2026-07-19, spread across
4 different teams/games) — not by market type at all in this window.

**What should we track after another week?** (1) Whether TEAM5 NO ever produces an
official-candidate row (score ≥ 0.40) once more dates are added, and whether the
weak-starter / 45–50-offense context cuts hold up past n≈70. (2) Whether `team totals ×
roughly_even_matchup` and `F5 winner × weaker_vs_stronger` persist past n≈150-200. (3)
Whether WSN coverage gaps continue (durable Kalshi-side gap) or resolve (was specific to
this window). (4) Whether YES 56–65¢/66–80¢ team-total and moneyline underpricing persists
at larger sample.

**What should we avoid changing?** No lane, threshold, score, or model logic — this is a
monitoring report only. In particular: do not treat the TEAM5 NO context cuts (starter
K-BB%, offense-form) as a reason to add a new lane filter; do not read the section-5 "fade
big moves" P/L as a tradable signal without the price-level control the base report already
flagged as missing; do not treat n=60-90 cells anywhere in this report as confirmed edges.

**Verdict: "Watchlist only; no model changes."** Two threads are worth deeper study on
their own time rather than immediate action: **"Run-differential context deserves deeper
study"** (`team totals × roughly_even_matchup` and `F5 winner × weaker_vs_stronger` are the
two cleanest new cells this tracker surfaced) and **"Expensive YES buckets remain
suspicious"** (56–65¢/66–80¢ still underperform breakeven, concentrated in moneyline and
team totals). Everything else — TEAM5 NO, brain-market disagreement, market drift — needs
more data before it supports any conclusion stronger than "keep watching."
